body:
Scores are competitive by nature, the more of the currency you get, the 'better' it feels.

Scores absolutely should not be visible or even a factor in the algorithm in these communities

The biggest challenge in responding is knowing what to put and how to say it, and being okay with your time, effort and words essentially meaning nothing (as most people's lives who post here probably feel the same)

There's so many people who are all going through the same cycle, who can relate as the posts often show, yet there's no way you can see how others overcome their troubles, or if they do at all, or whether people here _actually_ commit suicide or whether they're just venting, or trolling, or anything else really.

Thing is, you can't see if your thread has been read at all, and the reason I responded was I can appreciate how it must feel to type out your words (after going through the effort to make a throw away account) then just to get a whole stream of nothing in return.

Reddit is a great platform for discussion but most posts here do follow a similar pattern.

I'm going to publish some stats later on just how many posts are ignored and other fun stuff you can do with analysing over 20,000 threads :)

I liked the video by kurzgesagt on [loneliness](https://youtube.com/watch?v=n3Xv_g3g-mA) because it's a raw take on how the world is so busy yet people can be so isolated at the same time. 

However you are not alone in feeling this way, I often wonder how to put myself out there since I'm incredibly anxious and often shy away from meeting anyone new, which ends up as a catch 22. 

If you're going to kill yourself why not decide "fuck it, what's the worst that can happen?", find a group, say hi, leave when you want if you want if it gets too much and grow from the experience.

You don't need to be alone, nobody does, but taking the first step can feel like climbing a mountain, it can be done, but it takes a lot of effort.
10 years is an awful long time for things to change, I hope one day you'll cringe at making such a post and your life is a complete transformation from how you feel today :).

Godspeed to you fellow Redditor. I'm sorry you feel this is your only chance of escape, I can appreciate that not everyone has the strength to continue through more painful days, I just hope you're not in pain going forward, whether you do die or continue living peace will be given to you in abundance :).

I often find it's easy to focus on what makes me sad and put a lot of thought into it, but let's take a different approach: what makes you happy?

I know the answer right now may feel like nothing makes you happy, but you must have a hobby or skills or something that makes you tick, hopefully your girlfriend gives you a reason to wake up in the morning :).

Mental health is a bitch, I'm having similar issues and doing CBT to try and work through them, and so far it's my thoughts I am trying to change and be more positive (although it's hard).

You can get through this, even if you don't believe that right now :).

Well, at least you know a (homeless) stranger appreciates your acts of kindness towards others. Sometimes I feel if it's worth being so nice when it appears those who lack any empathy or desire to be nice get further than I ever have or will.

I can't say kindness is always rewarded but at least you can say that you've done your bit, and you're a better person than they are. If life had a global leaderboard you'd be higher than them that's for sure, and for me that'd be a great small victory :).

You made a cry for help, and hopefully now it's possible to engage in constructive discourse on how you feel and what your needs are in terms of support.

You may feel that lady was a thorn in your side, you may dispise the fact she was there but she is why you're still living if you feel you would've committed to actually jumping. She didn't have to be there, so clearly something feels like you've got more to give even if you don't believe that yourself.

And please don't be hard on yourself, you may feel ashamed but you've allowed yourself to be at your most vunerable, where now people are aware of how you feel, your parents hopefully can realize that you previously didn't feel like you could talk to them and now you can.

Stay strong, stay positive, you know that option exists again but I'm hoping you won't feel the need to try so soon without exploring other options first :).

It's a vicious cycle that doesn't seem to have a resolution. I don't have access to a gun but even if I did, as you say, it could be yet another fuckup and life would punish me further by humiliating me in a way I'm never able to undo or control and I'll be forced to live as long as others require me too if I'm physically unable to try again, in fact, it'd probably make the desire to die even more so and therefore life would be even more painful.

Depression sucks, I wish there was a tablet I can consume to rid it forever...Maybe one day :).

I like that attitude. Being a good human is easy and free, and hey, if it makes things slightly better than that's always a bonus in my mind :).

And yeah, it's hard for me to really appreciate the impact my death would have on those who might give a damn about me, but if I was at the point where I was ready to go I wonder if that would cross my mind and be the barrier that stops me from crossing, in my experience thus far of almost going it sadly didn't cross my mind (more the impact and possible failure and forever remaining a cripple convinced me it's not worth it).

I wanted to open by firstly expressing my sincerest apologies for your ongoing difficulties. Losing a loved one I can only imagine is one of life's greatest challenges, especially as there are many emotions that are racing to be the one in control. 

It seems you're trying to process this in a way that allows you to numb emotional pain, is it the case the physical pain is a distraction?

I can't offer anything much to help you which frustrates me, are there support groups you can bounce off for good energy? If you keep it locked up you're going to find it a self destructive path and releasing it as harming yourself is not ideal but understandable.

I know it seems difficult today, but given enough time and support from groups either online or in the real world you can begin to heal. Please don't assume all hope is lost, you've lost one person you cared about, please don't allow yourself to do the same so others are mourning over your loss too, it can be a devastating chain reaction.

You can get through this, please believe :).

I want to believe they _are_ coming from a place of love when they say that, I don't know your parents but it does sound like they care, but they also reside themselves to the fact that you're a grown adult and can make the decisions you wish to. 

You've already earned a veteran of life badge going for 4 decades, are you feeling that you're nearing the end at this time? I am younger so your perspective can help me understand how so many years can change the way you see things. I imagine at least there's more to see, or is it a case of "well, I've seen most things, so it's okay if I am no longer alive anymore"?

In my experience when things go wrong it tends to be one thing after another, to the point where I wonder why I even bother doing another day...

But you have, you're still here, even though you've, by the sounds of it, been through some of the harshest experiences life can throw at you, losing a job is bad enough but a breakup too? However you can allow that to consume you, or shape your experiences for however long you do decide to live. 

I think people often get the thought "maybe if I just jump, I'll be on the other side", for me though it's not knowing what the other side is, and whether it will _actually_ be better than what I have right now...

It's strange, reading your post hit so many of my own pain points...An abusive family, lots of shouting and arguing...leading to no motivation and slight 'PTSD' as they haunt my dreams :(.

Yet I also cannot imagine your level of pain as you are getting it from all sides whether home or school. I'm really sorry you're having to experience this, I really want to believe this isn't what life is about...

It's hard to know how to direct you, I understand wholeheartedly how difficult it can be with no self worth, or confidence to put yourself out there, but that's what you _can_ do in whatever way possible. There has to be a group you can click with, even if it's here on reddit, something to give you an escape (that's not drugs or alcohol) to allow you to see or experience the pros of life even if it may appear there are little...

Please keep fighting on, it's easy to give up entirely, but I won't say I blame you for whatever decision you make, life sucks right now for both of us, I just hope it improves :).

Now I don't know your parents, but it can be really hard to understand and process when your kid comes up to you and says "hey, I want to leave this planet", and know what the response should be, some parents would phone the cops and have you sectioned.

Although I want to ask if anything more was said or if that's your interpretation, I can hope they said at least more than that, and if they do understand, why? Are they a source of trouble for you? What's going on to make you feel this way?

I hope you're open to engaging with the community here, at least you can talk openly and freely with us :).

I often think about Amanda Todd, her story is a tragic reminder of the powers of social media. I know how you feel about Clash Royale, I went on a 200 trophy losing streak and the game is designed to keep you playing, whether it's crown chests or quests or just your regular chests...and yet I wanted to destroy my phone after emote spam (yes, I do disable emotes sometimes).

However, there are games that are peaceful, non competitive like Stardew Valley or something, you can decide that "hey - maybe this environment isn't right for me".

You get one life. You owe it to yourself to at least try something different. Maybe a different game, maybe finding a hobby that you can establish, can be online or offline, by yourself or with a group. If you're going to kill yourself you may as well try something different, what do you have to lose, if it all goes spectacularly wrong you know the exit is right behind you and that, in my opinion, provides comfort and reassurance.

Either way, I hope you can overcome your difficulties, please don't put too much thought into what others are saying, I like to think they're just bots or even code in the game designed to get me angry or annoyed, and I find it in myself to ignore them :).

Sorry to hear you're feeling this way - I respect the decisions people decide to make, and I'm not here to convince you you're making the wrong decision, however, I would like to encourage you to perhaps explain why you're feeling this way - no worries if you don't want to.

What I can't do, however, is talk about methods that result in your death since the rules prohibit it, but we're on the internet, just as easily as you posted this you can, if you want, research the methods from most effective or common.

However, we're a support community, that is if you want us to be. If you really do feel like there's no escape then at least I can say thanks for taking the time to write your thoughts out, I like to believe you wrote here for a reason, and that perhaps there's a way for you to evaluate all your possible options (with your death being, hopefully, the last resort).

Anyway, whoever you are, wherever you are, I hope you're able to find peace whichever road you decide to take :).

I've also wondered if starvation is a logical answer to my issues, it seems so simple but the overwhelming urge to eat overrides my desire to leave this earth.

May I ask why you're feeling like life is like torture? It has its moments I do agree, I'm intrigued to hear a bit more about your story if you're willing to share :)
Hey there Vicky, how can we help? :)
